title: Title Sequence: How to Make One With AI in 5 Steps
summary: Make a title sequence with AI: letters built into the world, shots that move one thing, and room for names, from real title designs made in Flick.
body_markdown:
### What is a title sequence?


A title sequence is the designed run of shots that shows a film's title and main credits, usually near the start. It sets the mood, and with AI you can generate its images and motion from prompts.


### What is the difference between a title sequence and a title card?


A title card is a single shot that shows the title. A title sequence is a run of shots with its own design, and it can include one or more title cards along the way.


### How long should a title sequence be?


Long enough to read every name you need to show. A single credit shot in Duro runs 10 seconds and the Still Time title runs 8 seconds, so a short film can use one shot rather than a full run.


### Where does a title sequence go in a film?


Often at the very start, or after an opening scene once the story has given the viewer a question. In a short film it can also come at the end, over a shot held still for the names.


### Can AI write the letters correctly?


Often, if you put the exact words in quotes and ask for them as written, but read every letter before you use the shot. Set small text and names in the editor, where spelling cannot drift.


### Can I make a title sequence for free?


Yes, Flick has a free plan with no credit card: 100 credits at signup, 200 more for joining the Flick Discord, and 100 credits every week. GPT Image 2 stills run on the free plan, while Seedance and Kling need the Standard plan ($20 a month).
